items.title: A per-centre charter budget reaches the landscape search and charters specialists and background firms around each centre, off by default
items.design:
AMENDED 2026-09-17 (cold review of BL-1030/BL-1031): the pins prove world/* through harness_params.hpp's hand-kept copy of app.cpp's new-game path, not through app.cpp. So app::start_new_game_prelude and poll_worldgen's validation run take NO behavioural change in this item: the budget pointer defaults to none on landscape_search_params, the app passes nothing new, and any line the item does touch in app.cpp is reviewed diff against diff with the copy in harness_params.hpp.

THE DESIGN IS IN THE DOCS: DIGITISATION.md § 1 (the budget charters the whole web; one specialist per centre that affords one, richest first; nation balance dropped; charters stay near their centre; no budget and an empty budget are today's world), CORPORATION_GENERATION.md Pass 1, GENERATION_STRATEGY.md phase 6 point 3 (the roster axis is skipped on a budget world). This item is the plumbing; no price is chosen and nothing ships a source.

SHAPE (from the 2026-09-17 seam map; the cross-check's corrections applied). charter_budget: points by population-centre entity id (ascending map), integer, entries <= 0 dropped, so empty and all-zero are one state that takes the legacy branch. charter_spend_params: firm price and specialist price in points (no shipped defaults; the search refuses a non-empty budget with a zero price), window radius 4 (the seat's population_radius precedent), province cap on/off. landscape_search_params gains the budget pointer and spend params; the search copies spend state per evaluation (threads share params). A new apply_landscape_candidate overload branches ONCE: null or empty runs today's calls verbatim; otherwise remove_specialist_roster then charter_web_from_budget. The 3- and 4-arg overloads and generate_corporations/generate_background_firms bodies are untouched. On a budget world the roster axis is skipped, never re-keyed: the axis count and the tag formula stay.

charter_web_from_budget (corporation_generation.cpp, new, reusing file-local helpers, editing no legacy body): centres by budget descending, ties lower id; home nation from tile_to_nation of the centre tile (none -> unspent, reason no_nation); region from nearest_region reconciled against that nation (mismatch -> the nation's nearest region to the centre, or the national-character fallback); a centre whose budget covers the specialist price charters one specialist (focus and ownership from the region, today's capital 400 +/-40%, no nation balancing); the remainder buys background firms by the existing gap selection under the per-resource cap 8, the province cap when on, and the 200-per-body cap; anchor rungs are the window around the centre tile (wrapped metric), then the centre's region window, then UNSPENT (reason window_exhausted), never nation-wide; leftovers counted by reason. RNG keyed per centre and role with salts that collide with none in use. The player is a seeded pick among budget specialists; with none, the report says no_specialists and nothing forces one (sprint 45 decides).

app.cpp and harness_params.hpp change together and both pass no budget, with a comment naming the missing source (Beat 1). The synthetic budget builder lives only under tools/verify. No save-format change, no Lua key.

DONE WHEN: requirements.json § charter-budget-seam, all rows.

RUN CONDITIONS: Release harness builds via `bash tools/verify/build_lua_harness.sh <name>` into build_gen/verify (MSVC /O2 — the toolchain every pin is bound to; never %TEMP%); serial, quiet machine, build tree quoted; tracked tables only via --out.

items.title: What a denser corporate web costs: player_seed_sweep charters a synthetic budget at 1x, 2x and 4x and times the search and the economy tick
items.design:
AMENDED 2026-09-17 (Ben, NR-889: measure first): the sweep also runs the per-resource firm cap KEPT and LIFTED on budget worlds. That needs a budget-path-only switch in charter_spend_params (e.g. resource_cap on/off, default on) read by charter_web_from_budget; the legacy Pass 6 body and every legacy digest stay untouched, proven by --digest-check on the pinned seeds. Report per density per cap setting: firms chartered, unspent by reason (no_gap should fall when lifted), the 200-per-body cap hits, search ms per evaluation and ms per tick. The NR-889 ruling is taken off that table.

WHY. DIGITISATION.md hard part 7 and § Open questions: the charter prices are measured against live-play cost before either is fixed. The only figures today are ~0.9 s per validation tick and ~1-2.5 s per search evaluation in Release.

THE WORK. --charter-budget synthetic --budget-scale 1|2|4 [--province-cap on|off] [--specialist-price K]. The budget is SYNTHETIC TEST INPUT, printed as such on every header line and never read for density-follows-cities: 1x charters today's chartered count on that seed (specialists plus background firms, measured first), spread over non-razed centres by seeded per-centre weights (never population), integer by largest remainder; firm price 1 point; specialist price from a small ladder (e.g. 4 and 8). Per seed per density: specialists and firms chartered, unspent by reason, whether any specialist exists, the largest one-nation share of specialists, search ms per evaluation at thread count 1 (round_ms), ms per economy tick over the 12 validation ticks and an 8-tick live window after the seat, shortlist size and the trailing-net spread. JSON via --out.

DONE WHEN. The table over the library seeds (at least the three the pin run shows fastest, all 16 if the clock allows) is checked in; a NEEDS_REVIEW entry puts the price readings and the specialist-count behaviour to Ben for sprint 45. A static check shows no `synthetic` symbol under src/.

items.author: Claude (found by the BL-1033 lane on 2026-09-17, flagged by its cold review; filed by the main session)
items.title: A copied world does not tick byte for byte as its original: find the unfaithful copy and make world copies exact
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-17 by the BL-1033 lane (charter budget cost), probing whether one pre-landscape world per seed could be copied per matrix row. On seed 28 a copied base world matched the BL-1031 pins at D_search and D_land, but after the 12-tick validation settle it digested D_settle 18F78EB9B2B20F29 against the pinned 265C48A23E313B1A — whether copied before the landscape or after it — while the original world, settled with a copied recipe_registry, matches the pin. So `world`'s copy is faithful as data and unfaithful as a program: something the tick path reads differs between an original and its copy. Suspected (not located): an unordered container whose iteration order depends on insertion/rehash history, a pointer-keyed cache, or a cache the copy constructor carries stale.

WHY IT MATTERS. The simulation is deterministic by standing rule. The landscape search copies the base world for every evaluation (landscape_search.cpp score_one) but only scores statically, so today's shipped worlds are unaffected; any future feature or instrument that copies a world and then ticks it (a what-if preview, a save-branch, a matrix instrument) silently diverges. The harness comment in tools/verify/harness_params.hpp above build_app_base_world is the only other record.

THE WORK. A minimal reproduction in a harness (build seed 28 in app order, copy, settle both, compare snapshot bytes per tick to find the first tick that diverges), then bisect the tick path to the reading that differs, then fix the copy (or the container) so a copy ticks byte for byte. DONE WHEN: the reproduction passes on the 16 library seeds with the BL-1031 pins unmoved; if the fix must change iteration order on the ORIGINAL path, that is a world-mover and needs Ben's re-bless authorisation first.
